Area Master i

The production areas and the order they run in. Sequence is the process chain — fabrication feeds hooking, hooking feeds pretreatment, pretreatment feeds coating, coating feeds assembly — and it is what the plan's chain checks read when they ask whether a stage runs before the stage that feeds it. The lines and cells inside each area live in Line Master and Cell Master.
Key and name are both load-bearing. Plans record an area by NAME (Fabrication Area) and the engine asks for it by KEY (fabrication), so changing either leaves rows already written pointing at the old one. Both warn before they change.
The engine's own stage list — which Item Master column holds each cell's std output — is still in code. Adding an area here gives it dropdowns, entry tiles and changeover rows, but not a planning stage of its own.
Seq

Line Master i

The assembly lines. Each one is manned by a contractor's crew, so it carries a default contractor — the one used on a date with no Line / Cell Assignment of its own. Back-area cells live in Cell Master; both are the same underlying master, so a code has to be unique across the two.
Skills are the item categories a line can build — one tick per category, from the Item Category master. Auto Plan will only put an item on a line whose skills cover that item's category. A line with no skills ticked can take any item, so planning keeps working until you fill this in.

Cell Master i

The back-area cells — fabrication, hooking, pretreatment and coating. A cell's area is what makes it available to that stage of the plan, so a cell with no area is planned into nothing. Assembly lines live in Line Master; both are the same underlying master, so a code has to be unique across the two.

Break Master i

Tea / lunch / dinner breaks per assembly line or back-area cell. Breaks recur daily and reduce that resource's planning capacity for the overlapped hours. Add multiple rows for multiple breaks.
Resource
Type
Start

Shift Master i

The shifts the plant runs and the clock each one keeps. Every dropdown, the planning grid, the printed sheets and the auto-plan engine read their hours from here. A shift covers whole hours: one starting 6:30 owns the 6:00 hour, because the plan is built hour by hour. The name is the identity — plans and history already recorded under a name keep that name, so renaming a shift here does not rewrite them.
Resource works as it does in Break Master: leave it on All resources for the whole plant, or name a line or cell to give that one its own hours for that shift — a pretreatment tank starting an hour early does not change what the assembly lines do. A resource keeps the plant-wide hours for every shift it does not override.
Resource-specific hours are applied to the printed shop-floor sheets. The auto-plan engine still builds its timeline on the plant-wide clock — per-cell hours in planning are a separate step.

Holiday / Week Off Master i

Plant holidays and weekly offs. Both types are excluded from planning — the auto-plan engine and Insert Plan treat an excluded date as zero capacity for the resource(s) it applies to, exactly like a full-hour break.
Holiday is a one-off date (e.g. a festival). Week Off recurs every week on the chosen weekday (e.g. every Sunday).
Scope: fill in Line / Cell to cover just that resource; leave it blank and set Area instead to cover every line/cell in that area; leave both blank for the whole plant.
Work window (optional): leave Start/End Time blank and the whole day is excluded, as before. Set them and it flips — the day is excluded except that window, which runs at full capacity: "even on a week off, we still do production" from, say, 8 AM to 2 PM.

Cage Master i

The cage types pieces travel in. Pieces per cage names the Item Master column that holds the figure for each item; loaded at and freed at say where a cage is filled and where it comes back empty, which is what makes the peak-hour cage check meaningful. Fleet is the default count offered when a new cage count is entered.
The key is storage. Cage counts are recorded as <key>Empty, <key>Fleet and so on — changing a key orphans every count already taken under the old one.

Changeover Time Master i

Minutes a resource loses when the item on it changes — the die change, the colour change, the purge. Leave Cell blank for every cell in the area, and leave the category boxes blank for every item. The most specific row wins: cell + categories beats cell, beats area + categories, beats area.
Recorded, not yet applied. Nothing in the planner subtracts these minutes from a cell's capacity today — filling this in changes no plan. Wiring it into the engine is a deliberate step, because it will reduce what every cell can produce.
